title: The True Story of BlacKkKlansman
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the film BlacKkKlansman and the true story behind it: Colorado Springs detective Ron Stallworth's 1978 undercover infiltration of the Ku Klux Klan with fellow detective Chuck Waite, the Klan's deep history in Denver and Colorado, Stallworth's phone calls with David Duke, the Duke lunch and photo, the movie's fabricated elements, criticism from Boots Riley, and Spike Lee's response. The episode closes with listener mail correcting the hosts on table tennis equipment terms.

segments.title: Opening banter and movie spoiler warning
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode about BlacKkKlansman, discuss their reactions to the film, and talk about its awards and cast, including John David Washington.

segments.title: Ron Stallworth's background
segments.summary: Ron Stallworth becomes the first African American officer in Colorado Springs Police Department history and later a detective, and he goes undercover for years.

segments.title: History of the Klan and Colorado
segments.summary: The hosts outline the three waves of the Ku Klux Klan and describe the Klan's control over Denver and Colorado politics in the 1920s, including officials who were Klan members.

segments.title: Stallworth's files and the Stokely Carmichael assignment
segments.summary: Stallworth reviews the Klan's history in files available to him, then attends a Stokely Carmichael rally undercover and meets him as the film depicts.

segments.title: Newspaper ad and first letter to the Klan
segments.summary: Stallworth answers a Klan classified ad in the newspaper in October 1978 using his real name, and the Klan replies by phone.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short break before returning to the story.

segments.title: Phone contact with Ken O'Dell and Chuck Waite's undercover role
segments.summary: Ken O'Dell calls Stallworth and invites him to join. Stallworth recruits white detective Chuck Waite to meet Klan members in person, and Waite is later admitted to the Klan and receives a membership card.

segments.title: Klan application and David Duke phone calls
segments.summary: The Colorado Springs Klan sends the application to national leadership. Stallworth calls David Duke, the Grand Wizard, and the two have cordial calls, with Duke unknowingly speaking to a Black detective.

segments.title: David Duke's political career and Charlottesville
segments.summary: Discussion of David Duke's later political runs and endorsement of Donald Trump, his presence at the Charlottesville Unite the Right rally, and the actor Topher Grace playing him in the film.

segments.title: Film versus real events: Duke lunch and photo
segments.summary: Stallworth and Chuck Waite both attend a lunch with David Duke when Duke visits Colorado Springs; Stallworth is assigned to protect Duke and a photo is taken. The hosts note fabricated elements, such as Chuck being Jewish in the film.

segments.title: Investigation outcomes and the bomb plot
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the investigation as information gathering, the prevented cross burnings, Klan members at NORAD, and plots against a gay nightclub and an army base, while noting the film's bomb plot was invented.

segments.title: Why the investigation ended and lack of arrests
segments.summary: Stallworth was nominated to lead the Colorado Springs Klan chapter, which led to the operation being closed. The hosts discuss why no arrests were made and the voice-change sinus incident.

segments.title: Movie changes: Duke never learned identity
segments.summary: Stallworth did not reveal his identity to David Duke as the film shows; Stallworth kept it quiet until his later memoir. The hosts note the difficulty of the operation.

segments.title: Boots Riley criticism and Spike Lee response
segments.summary: Director Boots Riley criticized the film on Twitter, arguing it omitted Stallworth's COINTELPRO-linked infiltration of Black Power groups and implied police and Black Power groups united. Stallworth responded, and Spike Lee later commented on cops in general.

segments.title: Endorsement and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts say the episode is not an ad but an endorsement of the film, and close the main discussion.

segments.title: Listener mail on table tennis
segments.summary: Thomas from Philly, a table tennis coach, corrects the hosts on pips and smooth rubber sides and on the term choppers instead of chislers, from an earlier episode on table tennis.
